rationale: Author-of-record round 4 (confirm) on fix commit 7cc6421a (worktree byte-identical at the reviewed commit; go build clean; full internal/hook suite green — 32 PASS including the two new regression tests; the timed-out-suite note below is a verification-environment artifact, not a finding against the diff). The small diff does exactly what the round-3 tally prescribed and nothing else: (1) NIL NARROWING — ReadState's old unconditional `hs.Mode == "" && hs.SessionStartedAt == ""` check was indeed independently reachable post-initialization (WorktreeMain's DerivationFailed arm leaves ctx.Phase empty — consistent with everything established in rounds 1-3: only WorktreeSpec/WorktreeBead got the round-1 non-empty backfills), and ReadState copied that empty Phase verbatim while ignoring DerivationFailed, so .beads-present + bd-outage + no-session returned nil and runPreCommit read a genuine outage as 'not initialized, allow' — a branch-protection bypass and the true fail-open MIRROR of round-2's fail-closed bootstrap bug. The fix routes DerivationFailed to the honest state.ModeIndeterminate sentinel (never empty, never idle — the round-3 tally's own prescription, a sanctioned widening of the sentinel beyond tail rendering), and gates the final nil-check on !derivationFailed. (2) NIL-PATH AUDIT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED — I re-derived every `return nil` route in the fixed ReadState: FindLocalRoot failure and BeadsDirMissing are the only two remaining, PROVIDED phase.ResolveContext never returns a non-nil error or nil ctx; I checked that proviso against derive.go directly — ResolveContext/ResolveContextFromDirWithCache have no error-returning path (filepath.Abs failure degrades to "."; every switch arm sets fields; the single return is `(ctx, nil)`) — so the commit's two-route audit is complete for the code as it stands. Defensive observation (non-blocking, recorded as a finding): the `ctxErr == nil && ctx != nil` guard means a HYPOTHETICAL future error-returning ResolveContext would leave hs empty with derivationFailed=false and re-open a nil route; treating ctxErr!=nil as a derivation failure would make the invariant robust to that future change rather than dependent on ResolveContext's always-nil contract. Not required for this bead. (3) TESTS PIN BOTH LAYERS — TestReadState_BeadsDirPresent_DerivationFailure_ReturnsNonNil reproduces the exact bisected fixture (.beads present, SetListJSONForTest erroring, no session) asserting non-nil + ModeIndeterminate, and TestPreCommit_BeadsDirPresent_DerivationFailure_BlocksOnProtectedBranch drives the REAL Run("pre-commit", &Input{}, ReadState, true) over a real git repo + real config with no injected stateFn, asserting Block — value AND decision, per the tally's two asks. Both PASS; the earlier round-2/round-3 halves (BeadsDirMissing nil; healthy-idle non-nil) stay green beside them, so all four quadrants of the contract are now pinned. Scope is exactly the tally-named file pair (hook.go + readstate_test.go); Deviations: none — accurate. Round-2's fix is not reopened: the narrowing only affects .beads-PRESENT failure cases, which sandbox bootstrap commits (pre-`bd init`, no .beads) never hit, and the commit records all ten previously-red no-short E2E tests still passing (428.9s); I additionally re-ran TestNextReadyGate_PositiveBead_ClaimsWithNoPromptNoRefusal without -short at 7cc6421a myself — PASS (ok cmd/mindspec 64.6s, exit 0) — first-hand confirmation of no reopen. VERIFICATION-ENVIRONMENT NOTE (reported for the audit trail, and the reason this verdict landed late): my full `go test ./... -short` run hit a 10m package timeout panic in internal/instruct (TestRender_NoDeprecatedApproveOrder hung at 45s in its idle leg, which exercises the bd-backed lifecycle scan) — but the process table showed multiple OTHER reviewers' full suites (`go test ./...`, `go test -short`, `go test ./cmd/mindspec/`) running concurrently on this machine against the shared dolt daemon, and the identical test re-run in ISOLATION passes in 2.21s. The round-4 diff touches only internal/hook, which internal/instruct does not import — there is no causal mechanism — so I classify the timeout as panel-concurrency contention (the documented reviewer-contention failure class from prior specs), not a regression of 7cc6421a. Verdict: APPROVE.

findings.title: Round-3 G1 fix confirmed: fail-open mirror closed, nil contract narrowed to the two pre-initialization routes, both layers pinned
findings.detail: The diagnosis matches the code history exactly (round-1 backfilled WorktreeSpec/WorktreeBead only; WorktreeMain's DerivationFailed arm leaves Phase empty; the old final check ignored DerivationFailed). The fix sets ModeIndeterminate on the DerivationFailed branch and narrows the nil-check; I independently re-derived the nil-path audit and confirmed its completeness against derive.go (ResolveContext has no error-returning path, so FindLocalRoot-failure and BeadsDirMissing are the only nil routes). Unit test reproduces the bisected fixture (non-nil, ModeIndeterminate); integration test drives the real pre-commit dispatch with no injected stateFn and asserts Block. internal/hook full suite: 32 PASS.

findings.title: Defensive hardening opportunity (non-blocking): the audit's completeness leans on ResolveContext's always-nil error contract
findings.detail: ReadState's `ctxErr == nil && ctx != nil` guard means a future change making phase.ResolveContext return a non-nil error (or nil ctx) would leave hs empty with derivationFailed=false and silently re-open a post-initialization nil route past the narrowed check. Unreachable today — verified against derive.go's single `return ctx, nil` — but treating ctxErr!=nil/ctx==nil as derivationFailed=true would make the invariant self-contained. Suitable as a follow-up nit, not a change request for this bead.

findings.title: Suite-timeout during verification classified as panel-concurrency contention, with evidence
findings.detail: My background full-suite run panicked with internal/instruct's 10m package timeout (TestRender_NoDeprecatedApproveOrder/idle hung at 45s — the leg exercising BuildContext's bd-backed idle lifecycle scan) while the process table showed several concurrent reviewer test suites sharing the machine and dolt daemon. The same test isolated: PASS in 2.21s. The round-4 diff is hook-only and internal/instruct does not import internal/hook, so no causal mechanism exists. Recorded so the tally sees the failure was observed, investigated, and dispositioned with evidence rather than ignored; it is the known reviewer-concurrency contention class, and argues for staggering panel test runs rather than against this commit.
